Triggers.value: People who look similar to the victims

Maladaptive Strategies.value: I detach myself from the memories

Threat.value: Having strong physical reactions when something reminded you of the stressful experience
I have difficulty falling asleep because I need to stay alert
Being superalert or watchful or on guard

Memory.value: When I try to explain what happened I lose the thread and cannot finish
When I remember the event I feel intense rage
Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning

Negative Appraisals.value: My beliefs about how the world works have been completely destroyed
My reactions since the event show that I am a lousy coper
The event happened to me because of the sort of person I am

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Inaction Guilt: I will never forgive myself for not doing more to stop what happened
issues.explanation: The inaction/self-blame item is hard to reconcile with the indexed trauma of childhood physical abuse by a caregiver. In a child victim context, 'not doing more to stop what happened' implies agency that is typically not clinically plausible for the same trauma profile; a more general shame/self-blame item would fit, but this specific omission-guilt wording is questionable.

Within the Threat node, 'difficulty concentrating' is not a threat appraisal but a general arousal/cognitive symptom. The other Threat items reflect current danger and hypervigilance ('strong physical reactions to reminders', 'need to stay alert to fall asleep'). This item weakens within-node coherence and does not match the node's formulation role as perceived current threat.

vignette: Kai had always been drawn to the work of a detective, driven by a desire for justice and control. But as he approached his late fifties, the memories of his childhood began to seep into his present, threatening to upend everything. The smell of burnt food wafting from a colleague's lunch could transport him back to the kitchen where his caregiver would punish him with scalding water. On those days, Kai would find himself avoiding eye contact with anyone who resembled his victims - fellow Hawaiians with dark hair and brown eyes. As he struggled to make sense of these triggers, Kai became increasingly detached from his memories. He'd start recounting the events of his childhood only to lose the thread, unable to finish the story. The rage that would well up inside him when he recalled those moments was overwhelming, making it hard for him to sleep at night. He'd lie awake, vigilant and on guard, as if waiting for the next attack. Kai's experiences had shattered his beliefs about the world - a place where caregivers were supposed to nurture, not harm. He couldn't shake the feeling that he was a bad coper, unable to deal with the aftermath of his trauma. And when he looked in the mirror, Kai saw a person who must have deserved such treatment - a flawed individual who attracted abuse. As these negative appraisals took hold, Kai's memories began to feel more vivid and intrusive. He'd be working on a case, only for something in his surroundings to bring back the full memory without warning. His reactions would intensify, leading him to become increasingly hypervigilant and physically reactive. The smell of burnt food could set off a chain reaction - Kai's heart racing, his senses on high alert. In an attempt to cope with these memories, Kai began to avoid people and situations that reminded him of his past. He stopped wearing the traditional Hawaiian shirts he loved, fearing they'd trigger another episode. But this detachment only made things worse - the memories lingered, coloring every interaction and decision. His colleagues started to notice a change in him, commenting on how distant and preoccupied he seemed. Kai knew he needed help, but the thought of confronting his demons was daunting. What if he wasn't strong enough? What if he failed to overcome his past? The fears swirled around him like a vortex, pulling him down into darkness. It was then that Kai realized he couldn't do it alone - he needed someone to guide him through this maelstrom of memories and emotions. The weight of his experiences finally brought Kai to seek help, as he struggled to reconcile the detective he once was with the man he'd become. He hoped for a way out of this cycle of avoidance and hypervigilance, a chance to re-learn how to live without being haunted by the ghosts of his childhood.
